newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mitra Rajasa says to meet 1997 net target.
newsitem.headline: Mitra Rajasa says to meet 1997 net target.

text.p: Indonesian transportation firm PT Mitra Rajasa said on Wednesday it was confident of meeting its target for net profit in 1997 due to high demand.

"Due to strong demand from our existing clients and some contracts from new clients, we expect to reach our target," Teguh Budi Arianto, Mitra Rajasa's corporate secretary, told Reuters. He declined to give details.
Teguh said the company had targetted a 50 percent growth in net profit in 1997 but declined to give figures.

In a report provided by its underwriter Trimegah Sekuritas during the company's initial public offering last January, the company said it expected to book a net profit of 10.46 billion rupiah in 1996 and 16.44 billion rupiah in 1997.

By midsession on Thursday, Mitra was up 275 rupiah to 2,300 rupiah on renewed market talk that business tycoon Jopie Wijaya was likely to take a large stake in the firm, brokers said. Wijaya has denied the rumour.
Teguh declined to comment on market talk of a possible link-up with foreign partners or the induction of local partners.
"Just like any other company, we are always looking for a possibility to expand our business. We had some talks with other parties but none of them can be confirmed," he said.
An analyst with a local firm said that he had heard Mitra Rajasa was planning to expand its business by operating city public buses and leasing aircraft.
"It is not clear if they will join with other parties on those planned projects," the analyst said.
Another analyst ascribed the rise in Mitra Rajasa to its cheap prevailing price.
"Compared with other transportation stocks, the discount is big. It has good fundamentals, so it is attractive," he added.
